provenance.summary: Committed before the baseline was captured, but not all fixed before measuring: a first measurement showed that seven of the nine discovery expectations needed revising, and a second commit rewrote them before capture. Six component queries moved from expecting a named first result to expecting the same first result as the catalog without patterns (firstWithoutPatterns): 'grid list' and 'virtualizer' already rank an example above their component with no pattern compiled, a ranking of the existing search model that no block causes, so the expectation changed for those two; 'button', 'image', 'link', and 'text' still rank their component first. 'collections' moved from expecting the Poster grid first to expecting it within the top three (expectedWithin), because a category term scores 20 points against the several fields of the components that mention collections; that ranks the Poster grid third, a known discovery weakness this baseline records and does not pass as a first-ranked result. The registry budgets are the existing command-registry.json tiers; the other numbers are judgement, and the only size looked at beforehand was the seed's own source (460 and 526 lexemes), which informed the headroom of variantSourceLexemes. BL1-B2 then added the hero, pricing plans, and account settings blocks. Its queries, the component queries for the new participants, and the new relevant ids for button and text were written before any of them was measured; a first measurement then showed two expectations were wrong, and they were revised before capture: "split hero" first expected the Marketing hero first, but the variant example id carries both query words, so the pattern is expected within the top three (it ranks second); "billing toggle" first expected the Pricing plans within the top three, but the Toggle component ids and names outscore any pattern for a component word, so it ranks ninth and is expected within the top ten, a known weakness recorded below. An earlier name for the settings block, Settings form, already displaced the Form component search, so the block is named Account settings. The collections blocks, Company records and Task filters, were added after the baseline. Their discovery queries and expectations (company records, records, companies, contacts, task filters, filters, filter tasks), the component queries for their new participants (table, tag group, menu, select, search field, each expecting the catalog's own first result), their seed set ids, and their ids in the relevant lists of the collections, button, text, and toggle button group queries were written from the blocks' intent in the commit that precedes the block sources, before either block was measured. Decision 0026 amendment 02: the Collections category gained Company records and Task filters, and every collections block scores 20 for the "collections" name query, so the Poster grid, which ranked third alone, ranks fourth: the Virtualizer scores 40, and the Avatar component, Company records, the Poster grid, and Task filters tie at 20 and sort by id. Its expectedWithin on that query moved from 3 to 4 in the pull request that adds the two blocks, keeping the expectation and the known weakness. No other expectation, limit, or budget changed, and revisedAfterFirstMeasurement is unchanged. The navigation block, Workspace navigation, was added after the baseline as the first block of its category. Its discovery queries and expectations (workspace navigation, workspace, navigation, side navigation, collapsible navigation), the component queries for its new participants (sidebar, breadcrumbs, avatar, each expecting the catalog's own first result), its seed set id, and its id in the relevant lists of the menu and text queries were written from the block's intent in the commit that precedes the block sources, before the block was measured. The category has no other block, so no existing expectation changes. Since Decision 0029 (which supersedes Decision 0026 amendment 02, cited above) a pull request may change a query, a limit, or a budget when it states the change and its reason before measuring and logs it in revisions below; no expectation is removed, a change made after its result was seen is also in revisedAfterFirstMeasurement, and a threshold is never changed to fit a failure. The revisions below record each change since the close-out as an exact transition (the query and field, or the value, with what it was and what it became). The agent composition blocks, Chat panel, Agent trace, Context sources, Approval request, Property inspector, and Quick find, were added after the navigation block. Their discovery queries and expectations (chat panel, chat, assistant, tabbed thread, agent trace, agent, trace, thinking, task rows, tool calls, context sources, context, sources, excerpts, citations, approval request, approval, request, question stepper, questions, property inspector, inspector, property, properties, quick find, find, quick, jump), the component queries for their new participants (message, prompt composer, tabs, icon button, markdown, activity, disclosure, code block, preview trigger, progress bar, radio group, checkbox group, checkbox, number field, command palette, list box, each expecting the catalog's own first result), their seed set ids, and their ids in the relevant lists of the existing queries were written in the commit that precedes every block source, before any block existed or was measured, and each rank they expect comes from the search scoring rules and the catalog without patterns, not from a result. Context sources is a Collections block, so it scores the same 20 as the other collections blocks for the "collections" name query and its id sorts before the Poster grid, which moves the expectedWithin of that query from 4 to 5 (logged below). Quick find is a Navigation block and no navigation expectation changes, because Workspace navigation carries the word in its id and name. The Tool calls variant example carries both words of "tool calls" and the Toolbar and Tooltip components match tool by prefix, so that query expects the pattern within the top ten and records the weakness. The variant source size limit variantSourceLexemes moves from 700 to 1000 because the conversation and agent blocks carry sample message and trace content; the revisions below log every transition. The seventh agent composition block, Recommendation (Conversation, with the Compact and Ranked variants), was added in a separate commit of the same pull request, before any of its source existed or was measured. Its discovery queries and expectations (recommendation, recommend, confidence, ranked), the component query for its new participant (meter, expecting the catalog's own first result), its seed set id, and its id in the relevant lists of the button, text, card, avatar, and radio group queries were written from the block's intent, and each rank they expect comes from the search scoring rules and the catalog without patterns, not from a result. Today only the Pricing plans block and its example match the word recommend, through its recommended plan, and they rank below Recommendation, whose id and name carry it; no expectation covers that query for Pricing plans. A first measurement of the six agent composition blocks then showed that one expectation was wrong, and it was revised in a later commit and listed in revisedAfterFirstMeasurement: "task rows" expected the Agent trace pattern within the top three, but the existing Task filters pattern and its two examples carry the word task in their ids and names and outrank any keyword, so the pattern ranks fifth and is now expected within the top five, a known weakness recorded on the query. Every other expectation held at its first measurement. On 2026-10-12, after that measurement, Andrew approved retargeting "task rows" from the Agent trace pattern within the top five to the Agent trace task-rows example expected first (expectedId, and expectedWithin 1); the original target was an imprecise expectation, and the pattern's fifth rank stays on the query as its known weakness. The two entries are in revisions below and the query stays in revisedAfterFirstMeasurement.

discovery.metric: precision at 3 of `search <query>`: results in the first three that are in `relevant`, divided by min(3, results returned)

queries.knownWeakness: A category term scores 20 points against the several fields of the components that mention collections, so the pattern ranks third alone. Every collections block scores the same 20 and ties sort by id, so the Poster grid ranks fourth once Company records, whose id sorts before it, joins the category. Context sources joins the category at the same 20 and its id sorts before the Poster grid, so the Poster grid ranks fifth.
The variant example id carries both query words, so the example ranks first and the pattern second.
The Toggle component ids and names outscore any pattern for a component word, so the pattern ranks ninth.

The Task filters pattern and its two examples carry the word task in their ids and names, so they outrank the pattern, whose keywords and summary can score only 20 a field: the Agent trace example ranks first, then Task filters and its two examples, and the pattern ranks fifth.

The Toolbar and Tooltip components match the word tool by prefix on their ids and names, so they outrank the pattern for it, and the Tool calls variant example, whose id and name carry both words, ranks first.

queryRules.expectedFirst: the artifact the query must rank first (a pattern query)
queryRules.firstWithoutPatterns: the query must rank first what the catalog without patterns ranks first; `component` names the component the query is about
queryRules.expectedWithin: the artifact `expectedId` must appear within that many top results

search.displacement: For every component, `search <its name>` keeps the same first result with the patterns compiled in as with no pattern compiled.

denseBudgets.registry: The command-registry.json tokenBudgets tiers: `list pattern --limit 1` and `get <pattern>` at brief, compact, and full, and `search <query> --limit 1` at brief, compact, and full for each discovery query that expects a pattern first. Tokens are lexemes of the dense rendering (countTokens).
